query: Bought a Dell laptop for Rs. 65,000 on Amazon. Display died on day 3. Service center says liquid damage without opening it and refuses replacement.

model_output.summary: You bought a Dell laptop for Rs. 65,000 from Amazon, and the display stopped working on the third day. The service center is refusing a replacement by claiming liquid damage without even opening it, which is an unfair practice and a deficiency in service.
facts_extracted: Bought a Dell laptop for Rs. 65,000 on Amazon.
Display died on day 3 of purchase.
Service center claims liquid damage without opening the laptop and refuses replacement.

options.title: Escalate to Amazon and Dell Support
options.description: Raise a formal complaint with Amazon customer support and Dell management regarding the unverified claim of liquid damage by their service center on a 3-day-old product.
pros: May lead to a quick resolution without legal costs
E-commerce platforms often support customers for early-stage defects
cons: May not guarantee a direct replacement if the service center report stands
options.forum: Amazon Customer Support / Dell India Support

options.title: File a Consumer Complaint
options.description: File a formal complaint at the District Consumer Commission seeking replacement of the goods or refund of the price along with compensation for deficiency in service.
pros: Legally binding orders for replacement or refund
Can claim compensation for mental agony and loss

citations.relevance: Establishes your status as a consumer since you purchased the laptop for consideration.
Defines deficiency in service, covering the faulty laptop and unfair refusal of service.
Empowers the consumer commission to order replacement of goods, return of price, or compensation.

missing_info: Unopened evidence or second opinion proving there is no internal liquid damage.
Written rejection report from the service center.
